Mark / Jasmine — read the matrix and BlueNorth's markup. High-level legal position and a proposed compromise below.

Our concerns with a one-way exclusion in favor of customer:
- It materially erodes Redwood's cap/liability allocation and is inconsistent with our standard MSA set.
- "Consequential/special" are amorphous; permitting a one-way carve-out invites exposure unrelated to Redwood's direct obligations.

Proposed compromise (language sketch):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, special, incidental, indirect or punitive damages; provided, however, that the foregoing exclusion shall not apply to: (a) a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations; (b) a party's willful misconduct or gross negligence; (c) Customer's payment obligations; or (d) direct damages arising from Redwood's failure to implement and maintain the security controls expressly required under Section X (Security Controls)."

Key points about (d): we will accept an exclusion carve-out tied to specific, contractually enumerated security obligations (and limited to direct damages caused by failing to meet those obligations). We will not accept a free-floating one-way carve-out for "data-related catastrophes" without tying it to precise obligations and real causal link.

If BlueNorth wants additional protection for third-party subcontractor failures, we can discuss a combination of (i) strict subcontractor flow-downs for security controls and (ii) higher insurance requirement rather than removing the mutual exclusion.

Next steps: Mark — can your legal team confirm whether they can convert their redline into the sketch above (i.e., tie exceptions to specific security obligations) or propose alternative narrowly-drawn wording? If so, we can route to procurement for the final commercial review. If not, we schedule the joint legal call.
